D018_m001.question: It's been about nine months now, ever since… everything fell apart. I keep replaying it in my head, those moments, over and over, even when I don't want to. It just pops in, out of nowhere, usually when I'm trying to focus on something at the restaurant. Honestly, that’s becoming a real problem. I used to be so driven, but now? Most days I struggle to even get started, let alone finish a menu. I feel like it's all my fault, that I could have done something differently. The anger is probably the worst part, it just simmers under the surface, and sometimes it boils over at the most ridiculous things. I find myself forgetting simple stuff too, like where I put my knife or my notes, and I think it’s because my head’s just not in it. And don’t even get me started on being touched unexpectedly – a hand on my shoulder in the kitchen sends me through the roof.
D018_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m002.question:
Well, doctor, it's been about nine months now, and things just aren't right. Ever since… what happened with that pile-up on I-5, I can't shake it. I'll be in the middle of reviewing a claim, and BAM, I'm right back there, seeing it all over again, whether I want to or not. It's like a movie reel playing in my head, over and over.

My husband tries to get me to go out, but honestly, I just can't. I used to love our dinner parties, but now… the thought of making small talk just exhausts me. It's easier to just stay home. Sometimes I find myself thinking about whether I could have done something differently, even though I know it wasn't my fault. And I'm just so angry, all the time. Smallest things set me off. My husband says I’m short-fused. I know it's not fair to him.

And my memory, it's terrible. I forget where I put files, even yesterday's lunch. It's so frustrating because I've always been so organized. Then there's the noise. A car horn, a dropped pen, anything sudden just sends me through the roof. I jump out of my skin; it's embarrassing. It’s not how I used to be.
D018_m002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m003.question:
"It's been... almost nine months since the divorce, and frankly, I'm just not myself. I'm a real estate agent, so I'm usually on my game, sharp, but lately, my head's just not in it. I'll be showing a house, talking to clients, and suddenly, I’m not there. It’s like I’m right back in that awful argument, feeling that same panic, even though I know I’m standing in an empty living room. It's so disorienting.

And honestly, I just don't feel… joy anymore. The things I used to love, like closing a big deal or even just a nice dinner out, they just feel flat. It’s hard to even pretend to be happy for my kids when they’re excited about something. I find myself constantly thinking about how things ended, and I can't help but feel like it's all *his* fault. He ruined everything, and I'm left feeling this awful shame, like I'm tainted somehow.

Even little things set me off. A sudden loud noise, a car horn, and my heart starts hammering. It takes ages for me to calm down; my hands will still be shaking long after the moment has passed. I can’t focus on anything, not even a simple conversation. It’s like my brain just can’t hold onto information. I just want to feel normal again."
D018_m003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m004.question: "It's been... oh, about nine months now, maybe a bit more, since that accident at the old school. Every time I smell those cleaning chemicals, or hear a loud bang, it just brings it all back. My heart starts pounding, and I feel like I'm right there again. I used to enjoy my job, seeing the place clean, but now... the joy's just gone. I can't even remember the last time I truly felt happy, not even with my wife. I keep replaying it, thinking about what I could've done differently, how I should have prevented it. The guilt just eats at me, day in and day out. It’s gotten so bad that even choosing what to wear in the morning feels like a monumental task. And don't even get me started on being touched — if someone brushes past me unexpectedly, I practically jump out of my skin."
D018_m004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m005.question:
It's been… I guess nine months now since everything happened. I can’t stop replaying that night in my head, doctor. It just pops up, unwanted, usually when I’m trying to focus. It’s making it impossible to study for my exam, the one I’ve been working towards for years. Honestly, even if I passed now, I don’t think I’d even care. All the effort feels meaningless. I keep thinking, if only *they* had done things differently, none of this would have happened.

I’m just constantly on edge. Every little thing makes me jump, and then my heart feels like it’s going to beat out of my chest. It takes forever for me to calm down afterwards. And my memory… I keep forgetting things, little things, like where I put my keys, or what I was just about to say. It’s like my brain just can’t hold onto anything anymore, like it’s too busy being terrified.
D018_m005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m006.question:
It’s been over a year now, like 13, 14 months, since the accident. I know it happened, but most of it is just a blur, like my mind won’t let me really remember. But then at night, sometimes I see flashes of it in my head, or I'll wake up sweating and shaking from a nightmare, but I can never quite piece together what the dream was about. It's messed up. I try not to think about it, try to just focus on my deliveries, but it’s always there, lurking.

Even when things go well, like I hit my targets for the week, I just feel… nothing. No satisfaction, no pride. My boss thinks I'm just lazy. And honestly, my fuses are so short sometimes. Just a car cutting me off, or someone complaining about a late delivery, and I can just explode. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and it takes forever to calm down. It’s hard to keep up with work when I’m like this.
D018_m006.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m007.question:
"It's been... over a year now, maybe a year and a month since the accident. Sometimes, if I hear a loud, sudden noise, especially anything that sounds like a bang or a crunch, my heart just starts pounding. I feel this wash of dread, like I'm right back there. I try not to think about it; I push away the memories, but they're always lurking. It’s hard to describe, but large chunks of that day, they’re just gone. Like my mind put a permanent block on them.

The worst part is, even when things go well at work, or I achieve something I used to be proud of, it just… doesn't feel good anymore. There's no satisfaction, no real sense of accomplishment. And my patience has worn thin. I snapped at a colleague the other day, actually threw my headset across the room when they questioned a call. I’ve never been like that before. It's like I'm constantly on edge, always bracing for something bad to happen, especially if someone appears out of nowhere in my peripheral vision or makes a quick movement. It’s really starting to affect my focus, which is a huge problem in my line of work."
D018_m007.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m008.question:
"Thanks for seeing me, doctor. It's been... well over a year now, like thirteen, fourteen months since the accident, and honestly, things just haven't been right. I'm usually on top of things, being an audit manager and all, but my head's a mess.

I try to avoid going near that intersection, or even seeing certain car models. If I do, my heart races, I start sweating, and it feels like I can't breathe sometimes. It’s like it’s happening all over again. I can remember bits of the crash, the sound, the impact, but other details are just blank, a total fog.

At home, it's rough. My wife tries to be supportive, but it’s like there’s a wall. I can’t feel that connection, that love I used to have for her or the kids. It’s not fair to them. And I’m so on edge. If someone touches my shoulder unexpectedly, I jump out of my skin. Lately, I've been snapping at everyone – my team, my family – just yelling and cursing without thinking. It's not me, and it's really affecting my work and my marriage."
D018_m008.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m009.question:
It’s been over a year now, a year and a month to be exact, since… well, since everything changed. I’m a government official, you know, used to being in control, keeping things buttoned up. But lately, it’s like my own mind has turned against me. I’ll be sitting at my desk, trying to focus on a report, and suddenly, I’m back there, reliving it all. It’s like a movie playing behind my eyes, and I can’t stop it. Then I try to push it away, desperately. I just don't want to think about any of it, the memories, the feelings… it's just too much.

Honestly, a lot of the actual event itself is just a blur now. I can’t quite grasp it, like trying to hold onto smoke. What I do know is that I feel completely cut off. My family – my sister calls, my nieces try to connect – but it’s like there’s a wall. I just feel… numb to it all, especially to any kind of affection. And my nerves are shot. The smallest thing sets me off. A sudden voice, someone moving quickly into my periphery – I jump, my heart races. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, like I’m going to explode. It’s made everything so difficult, my work, my life outside of it… I just can’t seem to function like I used to.
D018_m009.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m010.question:
"It's been... well over a year now, maybe closer to a year and a couple of months, since that call. I know exactly what happened, the broad strokes, but some of the details... they just vanish. Like trying to grab smoke. And honestly, it’s a relief sometimes, because when something reminds me of it – a siren, a certain smell, even just a flash of a dark alley – my heart just starts pounding out of my chest.

I've been trying to avoid those reminders, stay away from certain parts of town, even changing my route to work. My wife says I'm withdrawn, like I'm not really there anymore. It’s not that I don't care, it’s just… I don't *feel* much. The joy, the sadness, it's all just… flat. Everything just feels muted. And I'm always on edge. The smallest things set me off. My kids running up to me, a car door slamming unexpectedly – I jump, totally caught off guard. It's like my nerves are frayed, always waiting for something to happen. It's affecting everything, my job, my marriage... I just don't feel like myself anymore."
D018_m010.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m011.question: It's been… I don't even know, well over two years now, since that horrible accident call. I can still hear the sirens and the screaming, even when it’s silent in my apartment. I try not to think about it, try to push it all back, but then a certain tone on a call or even just the smell of exhaust late at night… it just brings it all flooding back, makes my heart pound like crazy. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, like a live wire. The smallest thing can set me off, a wrong word from a coworker, a rude driver. I just snap. And honestly, it feels like the whole world has just become a dangerous place, you know? Like, there's no safety anywhere. And the brass… they just don’t get it. They just don't understand what it's like to be on the other end of those calls, to feel like you could have done more, even when you know you did everything right.
D018_m011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m012.question:
"It's been a rough couple of years, doc, over two now, since that accident. I can't shake these dreams, you know? Every night it's the same thing, reliving that horrific crash. Sometimes I wake up drenched in sweat, heart pounding. It’s made me hate driving certain routes, or even seeing certain colored cars. I try to avoid areas where the accident happened; I'll take the long way around even if it costs me time and money.

Honestly, I feel like the world's just a dangerous place now, like something awful is always around the corner. And I keep replaying it, thinking about what I could've done differently, how I could've stopped it. It's my fault, really, I should've been more careful. All of this has made me so on edge. My temper's short, I snap at everyone, even my ex-wife when she calls about the kids. It’s really affecting my work and my relationships."
D018_m012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m013.question:
Well, doctor, thanks for seeing me. I’m not sure where to start, but for well over two years now, I just haven't been myself. Things have been… off. There are times, out of nowhere, I’ll feel like I’m right back there, like it’s all happening again. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like a movie playing in my head, very vivid.

Because of this, I go out of my way to avoid certain places or even conversations that might bring it all back. I've become quite a recluse, which is tough as a CEO. My wife notices it, too. I just don't see the world the same way anymore; it feels like it's a dangerous place, and sometimes, honestly, life just seems meaningless. I even find myself blaming others, replaying things and pointing fingers, which I know isn't fair. This whole situation has made me so short-tempered. I snap at my employees, at my wife… it's like I'm constantly on edge, ready to explode. It's really affecting my business and my marriage.
D018_m013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m014.question:
"Well, Dr. [Psychiatrist's Last Name], it's been about two years and a month since the... incident. I retired from teaching not long after, and honestly, things just haven't been right since. It feels like I'm constantly on edge. Sometimes, out of the blue, I'm right back there, seeing it all again, feeling every bit of the fear. It’s like a movie playing in my head, and I can't turn it off. Because of that, I try to stay away from the park where it happened, or even talking about anything that reminds me of it. My husband tries to get me out, but I just… can't.

And people... I used to love my students, but now? I just feel like I can't trust anyone anymore. It’s like everyone out there is a threat, or they’re all just waiting to hurt you. I even find myself blaming specific people for what happened, even though I know logically it might not be all their fault. And the anger, it’s not me. I’m usually so patient, but lately, the smallest thing can just send me into a rage. I snap at my husband over nothing. It’s affecting everything, my marriage, my peace of mind. I just want to feel like me again."
D018_m014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m015.question: I've been feeling off for over two years now, since that accident on the job site. It wasn't my fault, but I still go over it in my head a lot, wondering if I could've done something different. When I see safety vests or even just hear a loud bang, my heart starts racing and I get all sweaty. I try to stay away from anything that reminds me of it, which is hard considering my line of work. I used to be proud of what I did, but now... I just feel like I'm broken. Like I'm damaged goods. It's tough, doc. Little things set me off too. Someone bumps into me, and I just explode. It's not like me, and I know it, but I can't seem to control it. This whole thing's really messed up my life.
D018_m015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m016.question:
It's been over a year now, Doc, since the storm took Liam. A year and a month exactly. I can't shake it. Every time the boat rocks a certain way, or the wind howls loud, my heart just pounds out of my chest, like I'm right back there, clinging to the rigging. My wife, she tries to talk about it, but I just… I can't. I find myself avoiding the usual spots in town where the crew gathers, even the pub feels too much like a reminder.

And the guys, they look at me different now. Some of them, you know, they whisper about how I should have done more, how it's my fault we were out there so long. It feels like everyone's pointing fingers, even though I did everything I could. I just can't switch off. Even at home, watching TV with the missus, I'm constantly on edge, listening for every creak, every noise. I can't relax, not really. It’s like part of me is always waiting for the next wave to crash.
D018_m016.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m017.question:
"It's been... I guess about a year and a month now, since the accident on site. It replays in my head, Doc, all the time. Just flashes of it, usually when I'm trying to relax or even just working, like it's happening all over again. I try not to think about it, try to push it out, but it’s like a rotten wall that just keeps caving in.

Honestly, I mostly blame myself. I go over it constantly, thinking about what I could've done differently, what I missed. It eats at me.

And I can't shake this feeling of being on edge. Even when I'm home with Martha, or just buying groceries, I'm constantly looking around, checking corners, like something bad is always about to happen. It’s exhausting."
D018_m017.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m018.question:
It's been over a year now, a year and a month exactly, since... everything. I'm just so tired. I'll be in class, trying to focus on a recipe, and suddenly a memory of that night just floods my mind. It's like I'm right back there, smelling the smoke, hearing the sirens. I try so hard to push it away, to think about anything else, but it's like a broken record in my head.

And I can't relax anywhere. I'm always looking around, checking exits, scanning faces. Even in the grocery store, I'm watching everyone, just in case something happens. It's exhausting. I just want to feel normal again.
D018_m018.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m019.question:
It’s been over a year and a month now, and honestly, it feels like I’m constantly looking over my shoulder. It's like a movie reel playing in my head, on repeat, and I can't turn it off.

I’ve even cancelled plans with friends who wanted to go to places that remind me of what happened. I know it’s impacting my social life, but I just can’t face those triggers.

D018_m019.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m020.question:
It's been
over a year now, a year and a month since the accident. Sometimes, it feels like I'm back in court, but it's not the courtroom. I'm reliving the whole thing, the screech of tires, the shattered glass… It’s like a movie playing right behind my eyes, and I can almost smell the smoke. I try to avoid driving past that intersection, or even anything that reminds me of it – the news, talking about accidents with friends. If a conversation even brushes on anything similar, I just shut down.

My ex-wife, God bless her, she still calls. She thinks it's my fault, you know, for going to trial that day. Like I chose to be there. D018_m020.options:

    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m021.question:
"It's been almost a year now, eleven months if I'm being exact, since the accident. I just… I can't seem to shake it. I don't feel like myself anymore. I'm a Pilates instructor, I'm supposed to be calm, centered, but I feel anything but.

Lately, if I hear a loud bang, or a car honking aggressively, my heart just starts pounding out of my chest, my breath catches. It's like I'm right back in that moment, even when I know I'm safe in my studio.

And the anger… it's always there, just under the surface. My ex-husband tries to talk to me about co-parenting, and I just snap. It's not fair to him, or to our kids, but I can't help it. I'm so easily irritated by everything. The smallest thing can set me off.

Honestly, most of the time, I just feel numb. Like there's a wall between me and the world. I go through the motions, teach my classes, smile, but inside it's just… empty. It's like I can't feel joy anymore, not really."
D018_m021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m022.question:

D018_m022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m023.question:

D018_m024.question:
Well, Doctor, it’s been nearly a year now, about eleven months, since my wife passed. And truthfully, things just haven't been right since. I'm a retired man, a widower, and the quiet of the house used to be peaceful, but now... it's just unsettling.

D018_m024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m025.question:

D018_m025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m026.question: It’s been almost two years now, since the accident. Sometimes I still can't believe it happened. Rehearsals used to be my escape, my joy… but now? D018_m026.options:

    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
